processing: Raw pu-erh handling: pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried, then sold loose or pressed, with no ripening pile.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, as usual in Yiwu; the remote gardens and small output keep any lot limited.
appearance_dry: Long dark-green leaves from old but not very tall trees, generally pressed into cakes.
appearance_liquor: Clear golden yellow, typical of young Yiwu raw tea.
appearance_wet: Supple olive-green large leaves, typical of the class.
taste_profile: High aroma and soft liquor in the classic Yiwu way, with a fine texture, wild mountain character and layered flavour that feels both gentle and resilient.

brewing.notes: Use very hot water and short early steeps. Later steeps can be lengthened steadily, so do not stop too early.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year in small quantities, and its reputation has grown only recently, so most cakes are recent vintages. Spring lots are the ones to seek, and as raw pu-erh they can be drunk young or stored.
description:
Yishanmo lies in the Han section of Dingjiazhai in Yiwu, and has become a name to know over recent years. The draw is a continuous, hard-to-reach stretch of cultivated old trees, counted among the largest of its kind found in the Six Great Tea Mountains.

Getting there is part of the story: a three-to-four-hour motorbike ride over two mountains and then a walk. The trees are not very tall, but many are a century old or more, and despite the continuous gardens, total output is small. Processing is the usual raw pu-erh route.

Expect the fragrant aroma and soft liquor Yiwu is known for, with a fine texture and a wild edge. It rewards patience across a long session in a gaiwan, keeping the first steeps short.

A small harvest and a rising name make it a natural target for mislabelling. Buy from sellers who can speak to the garden and the season, and be wary of low prices.
history: Little is documented about when the Yishanmo gardens were planted. The name has become widely known only in recent years, and its large area of old cultivated trees is much of the reason given. It also appears in lists of the Gumanche area around Mahei, Luoshuidong and Guafengzhai.
